mainTopic: כבוד הבריות and the מת מצוה, why earlier generations had miracles, stories of devoted sages and עין הרע, and the start of the משנה on who is exempt from קריאת שמע.
overview: This amud opens at the end of a ברייתא. It teaches that a person on his way to do a מצוה may not become impure even for his own sister, but must become impure to bury a מת מצוה. The גמרא asks how human dignity can push aside a Torah rule. It answers that the פסוק 'ולאחותו' itself teaches this. It then refuses to build a general rule from this case, because it is only שב ואל תעשה. Next, רב פפא asks אביי why earlier generations saw miracles when his generation, which learns more Torah, does not. אביי answers that the earlier generations had מסירות נפש for קדושת השם, and the גמרא shows this with the story of רב אדא בר אהבה. Then come stories of רב גידל and רבי יוחנן sitting at the immersion gates, along with three explanations of why עין הרע has no power over יוסף's descendants. The amud ends as a new משנה begins: women, slaves, and minors are exempt from קריאת שמע.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: he must become impure for a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that even someone who may not become impure for his sister does become impure to bury a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he does become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a ברייתא that started before this section. It says a person who is not allowed to become impure for his own sister must still become impure to bury a מת מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the word 'ולאחותו' (in the פסוק about a נזיר) about a person on his way to do a מצוה, such as slaughtering his קרבן פסח or giving his son a ברית מילה. He may not become impure even for his own sister, but he must become impure for a מת מצוה, a dead body with no one else to bury it. This sets up the next question about human dignity.

keyTerms.meaning: An abandoned dead body with no one to bury it; anyone who finds it must bury it.

phrases.english: But he does become impure for a met מצוה.
phrases.notes: This finishes a ברייתא from before this section. 'He' is the person who may not become impure even for his sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מִטַּמֵּא הוּא לְמֵת מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a ברייתא that the גמרא quoted just before this section, as part of its discussion of כבוד הבריות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The duty to bury a מת מצוה overrides the ban on becoming impure.

steps.title: Why should dignity beat a Torah rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why burying a מת מצוה, which is about human dignity, should push aside a Torah rule, since no wisdom stands against ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Let us say: 'There is no wisdom, no understanding, and no counsel against ה׳!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's ruling. Burying a מת מצוה is about human dignity, and the פסוק says nothing outranks what ה׳ commands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא has used this פסוק before to say that human dignity cannot override a Torah law. So it seems strange that the dignity of a dead body can override the Torah's ban on becoming impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Why? Used to ask why a ruling should be so.
'There is no wisdom and no understanding' (against ה׳). A פסוק used to show that human considerations cannot override the Torah.
Human dignity, the idea behind the topic of this סוגיא.

phrases.english: Why? Let us say:
"There is neither wisdom, nor understanding,
nor counsel against the Lord!"

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי, לֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that one becomes impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Human dignity should never override a Torah law, because nothing stands against ה׳'s word.

steps.title: Here the פסוק itself says so
steps.stepSummary: This case is different because the Torah writes 'and for his sister,' which teaches that he must become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it is written: 'And for his sister.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that here we are not using logic to override the Torah. The Torah itself teaches the exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'ולאחותו' shows that only his sister is forbidden to him, but a מת מצוה is not. So the rule comes from a פסוק, not from human reasoning about dignity.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; a way of setting a case apart.
Because it is written (in a פסוק).
'And for his sister,' the word the exception is learned from.

phrases.english: There it is different, as it is written: "And for his sister."

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a special פסוק for this case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought dignity alone was overriding a Torah rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah itself teaches the מת מצוה exception through 'ולאחותו'.

steps.title: Can we make this a general rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning from this case that human dignity overrides every מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let us learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes taking this פסוק as a general source: if dignity overrides here, maybe it overrides all מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah shows that the dignity of a מת מצוה beats a מצוה, perhaps we can build a general rule from it. That would undo the 'אין חכמה' principle everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us learn (a general rule) from it.

phrases.english: Let us derive from it!
phrases.notes: Meaning: learn from this case that human dignity always overrides Torah laws.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיגְמַר מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in step 3 to suggest a broader rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: Limiting the dignity exception to the מת מצוה case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a פסוק shows dignity overrides here, the same rule should apply everywhere.

steps.title: Holding back is different
steps.stepSummary: No general rule can be learned. Burying the מת מצוה makes him miss פסח or מילה passively, as שב ואל תעשה. This does not teach that dignity permits actively breaking an ordinary Torah prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: A case of 'sit and do nothing' is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the general rule. In the מת מצוה case the person does not break a מצוה with an action. He just ends up unable to do one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Becoming impure makes him unable to bring his פסח or do his מצוה, which is a passive loss. That is weaker than actively breaking a prohibition. So we cannot learn from here that dignity overrides an active sin.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Sit and do not act': failing to do a מצוה, as opposed to actively breaking a law.

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא explains that the מת מצוה case is a שב ואל תעשה situation. So we cannot learn from it that dignity overrides an active Torah prohibition.

phrases.english: "Sit and refrain from action" is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposal of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes active from passive breaking of a מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Dignity overrides only in a passive, שב ואל תעשה case.

steps.title: Why did miracles happen to earlier generations and not to us?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי why the earlier generations had miracles while his generation does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: What is different about the earlier generations, who had miracles, and about us, who do not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question starts here. רב פפא asks אביי why earlier generations saw miracles and his own generation does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the theme of honoring ה׳ over other concerns. The answer, given in step 10, will be about how far the earlier generations were willing to go for ה׳. First רב פפא will rule out one obvious explanation.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
What is different about the earlier generations
for whom miracles occurred,
and what is different about us,
for whom miracles do not occur?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: מַאי שְׁנָא רִאשׁוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the legal discussion to a related story about devotion to ה׳.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why earlier generations had miracles and later ones do not.

steps.title: It is not because they learned more
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules out Torah study as the reason. In רב יהודה's time they studied only נזיקין, while we study all six סדרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is because of learning, in the years of רב יהודה all their learning was in נזיקין, and we learn all six orders.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא knocks down the most obvious answer. The earlier generation did not learn more Torah than his generation does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He shows that his generation studies more widely: all six סדרים compared to only נזיקין. So more learning cannot explain why they had miracles.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning, especially of משניות and ברייתות.
The סדר of the משנה dealing with damages and civil law.
The six orders of the משנה.

phrases.english: If it is because of learning,
in the years of Rav Yehuda
all of their learning was in Nezikin,
while we learn six orders.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם תַּנּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules out one possible answer to the question in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that more Torah study explains the miracles.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The later generation actually studies more widely.

steps.title: Even עוקצין was hard for רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: When רב יהודה reached certain laws in עוקצין, he found them as hard as the deep disputes of רב and שמואל, while we learn עוקצין in thirteen versions.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יהודה reached in עוקצין the law of 'a woman who pickles a vegetable in a pot,' or as some say 'olives pickled with their leaves are pure,' he said: 'I see the difficult disputes of רב and שמואל here.' And we learn עוקצין in thirteen versions.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings more evidence that the earlier generation did not know more. Even one section of עוקצין was very hard for רב יהודה, while his own generation knows it well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה, a great leader, struggled with a single law in עוקצין. Later students learn that whole מסכת in many versions. This makes the question stronger: they knew less and still had miracles.

keyTerms.meaning: A מסכת about stems and leaves and their ritual impurity.
The deep discussions and disputes of רב and שמואל.
Here: a version or way of learning the material.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הֲוָה מָטֵי רַב יְהוּדָה בְּעוּקְצִין,
phrases.english: And when Rav Yehuda would reach, in Okatzin,
"a woman who pickles a vegetable in a pot,"
and some say
"olives pickled with their leaves are pure,"
he would say: The disputes of Rav and Shmuel
I see here.
phrases.notes: He means this law felt as hard to him as the toughest discussions of רב and שמואל.

phrases.english: And we learn
thirteen versions in Okatzin,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הֲוָה מָטֵי רַב יְהוּדָה בְּעוּקְצִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more evidence for the point made in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the earlier generation did not learn more than the later one.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה's difficulty with laws in עוקצין, compared with later students' mastery of it.

steps.title: Yet רב יהודה's prayers for rain were answered at once
steps.stepSummary: When רב יהודה took off one shoe, rain came; we afflict ourselves and cry out, and no one pays attention to us.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yet when רב יהודה would take off one of his shoes, rain would come. We torment ourselves and cry out, and no one notices us.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his question with a sharp contrast. רב יהודה barely began a fast and rain fell, while his own generation fasts and cries with no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once learning is ruled out, the gap in miracles is still unexplained. The question is now as strong as it can be. אביי answers it in the next step.

phrases.english: Yet Rav Yehuda,
when he would remove one of his shoes,
rain would come,
while we torment ourselves
and cry out loudly,
and there is no one who notices us.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ רַב יְהוּדָה כִּי הֲוָה שָׁלֵיף חַד מְסָאנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב פפא's question by showing how large the gap in miracles is.
steps.kashyaTarget: Any explanation of miracles based on Torah learning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The generation that learned less got instant answers to its prayers, so learning cannot be the reason.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up אביי's answer in step 10.

steps.title: אביי's answer: the earlier generations gave themselves over for God's name
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that miracles came to earlier generations because they had מסירות נפש for קדושת השם, and we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב פפא: The earlier generations were ready to give up their lives to sanctify God's name. We are not ready to give up our lives to sanctify God's name.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finally answers רב פפא's question about why the earlier generations had miracles and we do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא had already shown that the reason is not how much Torah they learned, since we learn more. אביי moves the answer to a different area: devotion. The earlier sages were willing to sacrifice themselves for God's honor, and that is what brought the miracles.
steps.whatToRemember: Miracles depend on מסירות נפש for קדושת השם, not only on the amount of Torah learned.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the question from step 6. The amount of learning alone does not explain why miracles come; devotion does.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is אביי answering רב פפא's question.

phrases.english: The earlier ones would give over their lives
for the sanctification of God's name;
we do not give over our lives
for the sanctification of God's name.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קַמָּאֵי הֲווֹ קָא מָסְרִי נַפְשַׁיְיהוּ אַקְּדוּשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question and difficulty built in steps 6–9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did earlier generations get miracles while we do not?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They had מסירות נפש for קדושת השם, and we lack it.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה tears off a forbidden garment
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה tore a כלאים garment off a woman he thought was Jewish, was fined 400 זוז, and made a joke about her name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the story of רב אדא בר אהבה. He saw a woman in the market wearing a כלאים garment. He thought she was Jewish, so he tore it off her. Then it turned out she was not Jewish. They set his fine at four hundred זוז. He asked her name. She said, 'מתון.' He said: 'מתון מתון is worth four hundred זוז.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an example of the earlier generations' מסירות נפש: a sage who acted at once to stop what he thought was a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא did not stop to think about the danger or the cost; he acted right away for God's honor. Even after the big fine, he accepted it with a light joke. That shows how fully he was devoted.

keyTerms.meaning: A garment made of כלאים (wool and linen mixed together)
They assessed (set the payment for) her

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
phrases.english: Like this incident of Rav Adda bar Ahava:
he saw a certain non-Jewish woman
who was wearing a karbalta in the marketplace.
phrases.notes: A כרבלתא is a garment of wool and linen mixed together, which a Jew may not wear.

phrases.english: He thought that she was Jewish,
so he got up and tore it off her.
It came out that she was a non-Jew.
They assessed her at four hundred zuz.
He said to her: What is your name?
She said to him: Matun.
He said to her: Matun —
Matun is worth four hundred zuz.
phrases.notes: A play on words: מאתן in Aramaic means two hundred, so "Matun, matun" is two hundred plus two hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates אביי's claim with a real story.
steps.raayaObject: That earlier generations had מסירות נפש for קדושת השם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב אדא בר אהבה and the כלאים garment.

steps.title: רב גידל sits at the immersion gates
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל used to sit at the gates of the טבילה places and teach the women how to immerse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל used to go and sit at the gates of the immersion places. He told the women: 'Immerse this way, and immerse that way.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about a sage's unusual behavior. This sets up the Rabbis' question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב גידל placed himself where women came to immerse so that he could guide them in doing the טבילה correctly. The story describes his practice first, and then the Rabbis will question it.

keyTerms.meaning: The gates of the immersion place

phrases.english: Rav Giddel was accustomed
to go and sit
at the gates of the immersion place.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָכִי טְבִילוּ וְהָכִי טְבִילוּ.
phrases.english: He said to them: Immerse this way, and immerse that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב גִּידֵּל הֲוָה רְגִיל דַּהֲוָה קָא אָזֵיל וְיָתֵיב אַשַּׁעֲרֵי דִטְבִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story placed next to the story of רב אדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב גידל regularly sat at the immersion gates and instructed the women.

steps.title: The Rabbis ask רב גידל about the יצר הרע
steps.stepSummary: The Rabbis ask רב גידל whether he is afraid of the יצר הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis said to him: Isn't the master afraid of the יצר הרע?
steps.whatsHappening: The Rabbis challenge רב גידל's practice. Sitting near immersing women seems spiritually dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question attacks the practice itself. Being in such a place could stir up improper thoughts. For an ordinary person this would be forbidden or at least risky.

keyTerms.meaning: Master (a respectful way to address a sage)

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא קָא מִסְתְּפֵי מָר מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע?
phrases.english: Is the master not afraid of the evil inclination?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לָא קָא מִסְתְּפֵי מָר מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב גידל's practice from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב גידל's habit of sitting at the immersion gates.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being in that setting should expose him to the יצר הרע.

steps.title: רב גידל: they look to me like white geese
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל answers that the women look to him like white geese, so the יצר הרע has no hold on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: In my eyes they look like white geese.
steps.whatsHappening: רב גידל answers the Rabbis. The scene does not stir any desire in him at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger the Rabbis raised does not apply to him personally. He sees the women with no feeling of attraction, so his practice is safe for him. The answer depends on his special level, not on a general permission.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a general permission for anyone to sit there. The answer works only because of רב גידל's personal level.

phrases.english: He said to them:
They look in my eyes like white geese.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: דָּמְיָין בְּאַפַּאי כִּי קָאקֵי חִיוָּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the Rabbis' challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Personal exemption: the concern does not apply to him
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sitting there would expose רב גידל to the יצר הרע.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רב גידל the women stir no desire, so there is no danger.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן sits at the immersion gates
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן also sat at the immersion gates, so that the women would see him and have beautiful children like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן used to go and sit at the gates of the immersion places. He said: When Jewish women come up from immersion, let them look at me, so they will have children as beautiful as I am.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second, similar story with a different reason behind it. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן was known for his beauty. His aim was to bless Jewish families with beautiful children. This is a different motive from רב גידל's, who was there to teach.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan was accustomed
to go and sit
at the gates of the immersion place.
He said: When the daughters of Israel come up
and come from immersion,
they will look at me,
and they will have children as beautiful as me.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲוָה רְגִיל דַּהֲוָה קָא אָזֵיל וְיָתֵיב אַשַּׁעֲרֵי דִטְבִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to רב גידל's, with a different reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן sat at the immersion gates so the women would have beautiful children.

steps.title: The Rabbis ask רבי יוחנן about the evil eye
steps.stepSummary: The Rabbis ask רבי יוחנן whether he is afraid of עין הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis said to him: Isn't the master afraid of עין הרע?
steps.whatsHappening: The Rabbis challenge רבי יוחנן. Showing off his beauty could bring עין הרע on him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the worry is not the יצר הרע but עין הרע. Something beautiful that is put on display attracts jealous looks. The challenge fits his stated reason, which was to be seen.

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא קָא מִסְתְּפֵי מָר מֵעֵינָא בִּישָׁא?
phrases.english: Is the master not afraid of the evil eye?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן: לָא קָא מִסְתְּפֵי מָר מֵעֵינָא בִּישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's practice from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's habit of showing his beauty at the immersion gates.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Displaying beauty in public invites עין הרע.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: יוסף's descendants are above the evil eye
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that he comes from יוסף, and עין הרע has no power over יוסף's descendants. This is proven from a פסוק as רבי אבהו reads it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I come from the family of יוסף, and עין הרע has no power over them. As it says: 'יוסף is a fruitful son, a fruitful son עלי עין.' And רבי אבהו said: Don't read it עלי עין (by the spring); read it עולי עין (rising above the eye).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge. As a descendant of יוסף, he is protected from עין הרע, and he backs this up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עין can mean both 'spring' and 'eye.' רבי אבהו reads עלי as עולי, so the פסוק means יוסף's family 'rises above the eye.' That is why the danger the Rabbis raised does not apply to רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as... (a method of reading a פסוק in a new way)

phrases.english: He said to them:
I come from the seed of Yosef,
over whom the evil eye has no control,
as it is written: "Yosef is a fruitful son,
a fruitful son by the spring,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:22. The word עין can mean "spring" or "eye", and that is the key to what comes next.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abahu said:
Do not read "alei ayin" (by the spring),
but rather "olei ayin" (rising above the eye).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אֲנָא מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף קָא אָתֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the Rabbis' challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Personal exemption, supported by a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's beauty on display would draw עין הרע.
steps.terutzMaskana: As יוסף's descendant, he is above עין הרע, as the פסוק shows when read as עולי עין.

steps.title: A second source: יוסף's descendants are like fish
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא proves the same idea from 'וידגו': like fish hidden under water, יוסף's descendants are safe from עין הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: We learn it from here: 'And may they multiply like fish (וידגו) in the midst of the land.' Just as fish in the sea are covered by water, and עין הרע has no power over them, so too עין הרע has no power over יוסף's descendants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different פסוק as a second source for the same idea, that יוסף's family is protected from עין הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וידגו, which יעקב said in his blessing to יוסף's sons, comes from דג, a fish. Fish live hidden under the water, out of sight, so no eye can harm them. The same protection is given to יוסף's descendants. The conclusion matches רבי אבהו's; only the source is different.

keyTerms.meaning: And may they multiply (related to the word דָּג, fish)

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources show that עין הרע has no power over יוסף's descendants: עולי עין (רבי אבהו) and וידגו like fish (רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא).

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אֲמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said: from here:
"And may they multiply abundantly in the midst of the land,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 48:16. The word וידגו sounds like דג, a fish, and the proof is built on that.

phrases.english: just as the fish in the sea,
water covers them
and the evil eye has no control over them,
so too the seed of Yosef:
the evil eye has no control over them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אֲמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק for the same idea taught in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That עין הרע has no power over יוסף's descendants.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 48:16, וידגו, compared to fish covered by water.

steps.title: Another reason: יוסף's eye did not take what was not his
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a second, reasoning-based explanation of why עין הרע has no power over יוסף. His eye refused to enjoy what did not belong to him, so the evil eye cannot control him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say it this way: an eye that did not want to feast on something that was not its own cannot be ruled by the evil eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to explain why יוסף's descendants are safe from עין הרע. This time the reason is not a פסוק but יוסף's own good behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 17 and 18 used פסוקים to show that יוסף's descendants are protected. Here the reason is measure for measure: יוסף kept his eyes from what was forbidden to him, so other people's eyes cannot harm him. This finishes the answer to the Rabbis' question to רבי יוחנן in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: brings in another explanation

steps.whatToRemember: There are two kinds of reasons that יוסף's descendants are safe from עין הרע: the פסוקים in steps 17 and 18, and יוסף's own goodness in not looking at what was not his.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
an eye that did not want
to feast on what was not his
phrases.notes: This means יוסף's eye, which turned away from פוטיפר's wife.

phrases.english: the evil eye has no power over him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another explanation, alongside the פסוק-based proofs of steps 17 and 18, for why יוסף's descendants are immune to עין הרע.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative reasoning (measure for measure) instead of a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Rabbis worried that sitting in public would expose רבי יוחנן to עין הרע.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because יוסף's eye did not take what was not his, the evil eye has no power over him or his descendants, so רבי יוחנן was not in danger.

steps.title: New משנה: women, slaves, and minors are exempt from קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. It rules that women, slaves, and minors do not have to say קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Women, slaves, and minors are exempt from reciting שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The story section is over, and a new משנה opens. It begins listing groups of people who are exempt from certain מצוות, starting with קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, not part of the רבי יוחנן story. The משנה names three groups together, women, slaves, and minors, and states that they are פטור from קריאת שמע. The משנה continues past these words with more מצוות, and the גמרא will explain the reasons later.
steps.confusionAlert: Being פטור only means these people are not obligated to say שמע. It does not mean they are forbidden to say it.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Women, slaves, and minors
are exempt from reciting שמע

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים פְּטוּרִין מִקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the story about רבי יוחנן is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women, slaves, and minors are exempt from קריאת שמע.
